Pursuant to Section 3-05 of the New York City Procurement Policy Board Rules, the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) intends to enter into negotiations for a six-year agreement with Biolytical Laboratories Inc. to provide INSTI® HIV-1/HIV-2 Rapid Antibody Tests and INSTI® HIV-1/HIV-2 Test Controls on an as needed basis. These products will be utilized by DOHMH's Bureau of HIV's Field Services Unit and in DOHMH`s Sexually Transmitted Disease (STD) Clinics throughout NYC for rapid detection of HIV antibodies.  

DOHMH has determined that Biolytical Laboratories Inc. is the sole source provider of these products. BioLytical Laboratories Inc. is the sole manufacturer and seller of the branded INSTI® HIV Test, all INSTI® HIV Test products are manufactured and sold exclusively by BioLytical Laboratories Inc. and must be purchased directly from them. There are no resellers or distributors for these products. 

Any firm that believes it can legally provide these goods, is invited to submit an Expression of Interest directly to this RFI- EPIN 81627Y0870 no later than 10/23/2026 by 2:00PM.

In accordance with Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) of the Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the Department of Probation (DOP) is requesting approval to extend the existing contract with Good Shepherd Services, (GSS) through a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) to support the continuation of services under the Advocate, Intervene, Mentor (AIM) Program. The contract term is from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2028 in the amount of 2,145,203.52 for this period.

Advocate-mentors are credible messengers with strong ties to the communities served and lived experience that enables effective engagement with participants. Design and Construction | Procurement | Award | $8.7M | Vendor: XBR Inc. item.title: Gender Affirming Care
item.description:
Health and Mental Hygiene | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-10-16 In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene intends to negotiate contracts with Callen-Lorde and Nonprofit Organization for Philanthropic Initiatives for gender-affirming care for patients under 18, estimated at $8,879,218 through June 30, 2029.

Pursuant to PPB Rule 3-04(b)(2)(i)(D), the NYC Health Department intends to process a Negotiated Acquisition solicitation as there is a compelling need for gender-affirming care services that cannot be met timely by competitive sealed proposals. NYC Health will contract with organizations providing or facilitating the provision of gender-affirming care to patients under age 18. This includes the prescription and administration of puberty-blockers and hormone replacement therapy to all minor patients for whom such services are medically necessary based on the prevailing standards of care. Services will be performed by qualified medical providers with current New York State licensure, and will be provided consistent with state laws governing parental consent. 

The proposed contract term for each contract is three (3) years, with a proposed start date of February 01, 2027 to June 30, 2029, with one three-year option to renew. The total estimated procurement value?is $8,879,218.00.

item.title: NDA Healthy Families NAQ
item.description:
Youth and Community Development | Procurement | Award | $277K | Vendor: Crown Heights Jewish Community Council Inc In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Youth and Community Development awarded Crown Heights Jewish Community Council Inc. a $276,578 contract, negotiated with one vendor rather than open competition, for Healthy Families services in low-income neighborhoods.

The Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD), as the designated Community Action Agency for New York City, administers the federal Community Services Block Grant (CSBG) program to combat poverty and provide services that empower low-income individuals and families to achieve self-sufficiency. To maximize the impact of CSBG funding, DYCD targets funds to low-income neighborhoods designated as Neighborhood Development Areas (NDAs). The NDA Initiative promotes community-level engagement to ensure that services address the most pressing needs within each community. Programs use a strength-based approach, partnering with participants to build upon existing assets and capacities to achieve personal and community goals. Given the specialized nature of these services and the need for continuity and responsiveness to local community conditions, DYCD seeks approval to use the Negotiated Acquisition method in accordance with PPB Rule §3-04(b)(2)(i)(D). This approach allows the agency to negotiate directly with qualified community-based organizations (CBOs) that have demonstrated experience, trust, and engagement within their respective NDAs.

item.title: DOP FY27-28 AIM Program Contract with UYAI
item.description:
Probation | Procurement | Award | $2.1M | Vendor: Urban Youth Alliance International Inc. In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Probation extended its contract with Urban Youth Alliance International Inc. for $2,068,000 to run July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2028, to continue the Advocate, Intervene, Mentor program, which provides one-on-one community mentoring for high-risk youth on probation.

In accordance with Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) of the Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the New York City Department of Probation (DOP) has extended its contract with Urban Youth Alliance International, Inc. (UYAI) through a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) for continued services under the Advocate, Intervene, Mentor (AIM) Program. The contract term is July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2028, in the amount of $2,068,000.00.

The AIM Program is an Alternative to Placement (ATP) intervention for high-risk, justice-involved youth on probation. AIM provides intensive, community-based, one-on-one mentoring through paid advocate-mentors who serve as consistent supports to participants. Services focus on improving decision-making, strengthening family and community connections, and reducing further justice system involvement.

item.title: NOTICE OF INTENT PRE-EMPLOYMENT PSYCHOLOGICAL EXAMINATION SERVICES
item.description:
Probation | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-10-16 In plain English (machine-written): The Department of Probation intends to award a $110,350 contract to Institute for Forensic Psychology, without open competition, for pre-employment psychological exams of Probation Officer candidates, covering July 1, 2025 through Sept. 30, 2026.

The New York City Department of Probation (DOP) intends to enter into a Negotiated Acquisition with Institute for Forensic Psychology (IFP) for the provision of specialized pre-employment psychological examination and evaluation services for Probation Officer candidates.

The anticipated contract term is July 1, 2025 through September 30, 2026, with a total not-to-exceed amount of $110,350.00.

DOP is utilizing the Negotiated Acquisition method pursuant to PPB Rule § 3-04(b)(2)(i)(D) due to a time-sensitive and compelling need for these specialized services that could not timely be met through competitive sealed bidding or competitive sealed proposals. DOP requires continued access to qualified psychological professionals with specialized experience conducting law-enforcement and public-safety suitability assessments in order to timely evaluate Probation Officer candidates and support agency staffing and operations.

Organizations that believe they are qualified to provide the same or similar services may express interest in this procurement, or in future solicitations for these services, by contacting Chairon Jeffrey, Deputy ACCO, at CJeffrey@probation.nyc.gov.
